chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah is more Majestic and more Magnificent than that He would leave the earth without a just Imam.

key_terms.أَجَلّ: More Majestic/Loftier — attributes of divine transcendence implying that God's perfection demands purposeful governance of creation
key_terms.أَعْظَم: More Magnificent/Greater — a second superlative reinforcing divine greatness beyond the possibility of negligence
key_terms.إِمَام عَادِل: Just Imam — the divinely appointed Imam possessing justice ('adl), a key attribute in Shia theology distinguishing legitimate Imams from unjust rulers

ai.seo_question: Does Islam teach that the earth always has a divinely appointed Imam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) asserts a fundamental creedal principle: Divine transcendence necessitates the perpetual existence of a just Imam on earth. The argument is a reductio — it would be beneath God's majesty to abandon humanity without authoritative guidance. This was taught in the context of Shia theological debates about the necessity of the Imamate, affirming that the earth is never without a divinely appointed guide.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more Majestic and More Magnificent than that He<sup>azwj</sup> would Leave the earth without a Just Imam<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu Hamza from abu Basir from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following “
Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, is far greater and above leaving the earth without an Imam of justice.”
